chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Hafs, from Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir, from Salim ibn Abu Ja'dah. He said:

I heard Ka'b al-Ahbar saying: Indeed, it is in our book that a man from the offspring of Muhammad, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), will be killed, and the sweat of the riding animals of his companions shall not dry until they enter Paradise and embrace the wide-eyed houris. Then al-Hasan (peace be upon him) passed by us and we said: Is he this one? He said: No. Then al-Husayn (peace be upon him) passed by us and we said: Is he this one? He said: Yes.

key_terms.الحور العين: The wide-eyed houris, companions of Paradise described in Islamic eschatology
key_terms.كعب الأحبار: Ka'b al-Ahbar, a Jewish rabbi who converted to Islam and was known for relating prophecies from previous scriptures

ai.seo_question: Did Ka'b al-Ahbar prophecy the martyrdom of Imam Husayn from Jewish scriptures?
ai.summary: Ka'b al-Ahbar, a prominent Jewish convert to Islam known for his knowledge of previous scriptures, relates a prophecy from his book that a descendant of Prophet Muhammad (S) will be martyred, and his companions will enter Paradise so swiftly that their mounts' sweat will not even dry. When al-Hasan (AS) passes, Ka'b denies he is the one; when al-Husayn (AS) passes, Ka'b confirms he is the prophesied martyr. This narration was shared during Muharram commemorations, underscoring the foreknowledge of Imam Husayn's martyrdom even in pre-Islamic scriptures.
